PullRequest.Title: Fix/64292
PullRequest.Body:
Missing checks for custom titlebar / native menubar (macOS). I can't actually test this on macOS as I am unable to make it into the office for a few days.

fixes #64292

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The resize-to-layout call chain and the synchronous DOM reads/writes are explicit in repository code. The exact millisecond cost varies by platform and extension-contributed menu state, but execution on every resize event is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM reconstruction, synchronous style/layout calculation, and transient SubmenuAction objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the number of raw resize events and top-level menus; overflow additionally allocates actions for each hidden top-level menu on every event.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher synchronous resize latency, CPU/GC pressure, and dropped resize frames
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, MenubarControl.layout only set the container height and adjusted visibility; it did not rebuild labels or scan menu widths on each workbench layout.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every titlebar layout now calls MenuBar.update, which rewrites every top-level label and synchronously recalculates overflow.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call at MenubarControl.layout line 605 places MenuBar.update on every titlebar layout; the deleted implementation at the same method only updated height and visibility.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding the menubar on every resize layout
Findings.Impact: Dragging the window edge can spend each raw resize event rebuilding menu DOM, forcing layout, and allocating overflow actions, increasing resize latency and causing visible frame drops.
Findings.Evidence: Electron's window resize listener calls shell.layout synchronously; WorkbenchLayout then calls titlebar.layout, which reaches this added line. MenuBar.update assigns innerHTML for every cached menu and calls updateOverflowAction; that method reads container/menu offsetWidth values while changing visibility and moving the overflow node, so style/layout work is forced on the resize critical path. When overflow is active it also recreates one SubmenuAction per hidden top-level menu.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep resize handling to an overflow-only layout method, cache the last available width, and skip work when it is unchanged. Update labels only when mnemonic/options change, and batch width reads before visibility/node writes (or coalesce the relayout to one animation frame).

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a window using the custom titlebar and custom menubar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each raw window resize event synchronously calls Shell.layout, WorkbenchLayout.layout, TitlebarPart.layout, MenubarControl.layout, and the newly added MenuBar.update before the resize handler returns.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Raw resize-event frequency multiplied by the fixed set of top-level menus (normally eight); when space is constrained, work also scales with the number of hidden top-level menus.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the renderer UI thread with no animation-frame coalescing for normal resize events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no unchanged-width or unchanged-options fast path. Labels are rewritten and overflow is recomputed on every layout, including warm repeated layouts at the same effective width.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event-to-layout call chain and the innerHTML writes, offsetWidth/getBoundingClientRect reads, visibility writes, node moves, and overflow-action allocation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame loss depends on platform, resize event rate, and renderer load; top-level cardinality is bounded, so severity is medium rather than high.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the diff moves full synchronous menubar update work onto every resize layout, whereas the old layout path only adjusted height and visibility.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create the custom menubar during workbench startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MenubarControl.create synchronously constructs MenuBar, traverses each top-level menu and nested submenu action graph, creates top-level DOM buttons, and applies styling before titlebar setup completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eight built-in top-level menus plus extension-contributed actions and nested submenu entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer work; submenu action graphs are traversed serially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: One cold construction per titlebar instance. The action arrays then act as the current menu snapshot and are replaced on menu changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for synchronous construction and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension-contributed menu size varies, but the traversal was already present in the previous custom-menubar setup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the refactor preserves the existing eager startup traversal and DOM creation rather than materially amplifying it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, hover between, and navigate custom menus including the overflow menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening constructs a Menu widget and action-item DOM synchronously; hovering to another top-level menu disposes the current widget and constructs the next one. Opening an overflow entry can construct a nested submenu and measure its bounds.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible actions in the selected menu; overflow adds one submenu entry for each hidden top-level menu, with nested work only for the selected entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on input events in the renderer; no IPC, filesystem, database, network, or subprocess operations are performed by menu rendering itself.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu widgets are rebuilt per opening rather than cached. This behavior already existed for ordinary top-level menus; overflow metadata is regenerated during overflow layout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for DOM construction and disposal paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual menu sizes and interaction frequency vary; no diff-introduced unbounded cardinality was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: per-open reconstruction and retained-disposable registration existed before the refactor, while overflow submenu creation is bounded by the small top-level menu set.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh a custom menubar after configuration, keybinding, update-state, menu, recent-item, or maximize changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Most events schedule one RunOnceScheduler callback after 200 ms; setupCustomMenubar then rebuilds action snapshots. Individual IMenu changes on the custom path also rebuild only that top-level menu immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the recently opened workspace/file list
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per windowsService recently-opened change event, followed by one coalesced menubar refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same getRecentlyOpened request was made on this event before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The promise completion gates updating the recent-action snapshot, but not unrelated UI progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Event bursts after scheduler coalescing, multiplied by all top-level menus for scheduled full refreshes or one changed menu for direct menu notifications.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer-thread rebuild at a time; the RunOnceScheduler coalesces scheduled bursts, while direct per-menu updates remain synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current action arrays are cached on MenuBar entries, but a refresh traverses authoritative menu state again. No negative-cache behavior applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for scheduling and action traversal; no new high-frequency external boundary was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu-change frequency depends on extensions and context changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: scheduled refresh remains coalesced, the recently-opened IPC is unchanged, and the new maximize-triggered rebuild is rare.

Scenarios.Scenario: Synchronize the native macOS/native-titlebar menubar after menu-affecting events
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A 200 ms scheduler coalesces events, then the renderer serializes all top-level menu/submenu items and keybindings and sends one menubar update to the main process.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the complete native menubar model to the Electron main process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC for each 200 ms-coalesced update burst, independent of the number of top-level menus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, doSetupMenubar built the same complete native model and issued one updateMenubar IPC per coalesced burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The send occurs after synchronous serialization; it is not on custom-menubar resize or menu-open paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is one IPC per coalesced event burst; payload size scales with all menu actions and nested submenu entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized menu traversal followed by one IPC request; RunOnceScheduler prevents concurrent fan-out from event bursts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No payload cache is used, but scheduler coalescing preserves the existing warm-event behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the service interface and call site establish a single renderer-to-main boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Payload size depends on installed extension contributions, but the diff does not increase boundary cardinality or move it to resize.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: native IPC cardinality, coalescing, and full-model serialization are preserved.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and traced custom-menubar creation, resize/layout, menu opening and overflow navigation, dynamic menu refresh, recently-opened refresh, and native-menubar synchronization. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity performance finding for full menubar DOM/overflow work newly placed on every raw window-resize layout. Native IPC and recently-opened IPC retain their pre-diff cardinality; menu-open cleanup retention is pre-existing rather than PR-caused.
